a benchmark of 400 expert-curated tasks spanning Law, Finance, Industry, Healthcare, and Natural Science
We adopt a rubric-based evaluation protocol scoring factual accuracy, logical coherence, practical feasibility, and professional compliance
together, $OMB provides a unified testbed for assessing agentic reliability, professional depth, and an indicator of practical readiness in domain-intensive scenarios
existing benchmarks remain largely confined to structured or exam-style tasks that fall short of real-world professional demands
curated through a collaborative effort spanning over 2,000 expert hours
The estimated value of all tasks exceeds $1 million, giving the benchmark its name.
The benchmark comprises 400 challenging open-ended tasks in five domains: Finance, Law, Healthcare, Natural Science, and Industry

a senior actuary auditing a life-insurance reserve valuation under IFRS 17; an M&A lawyer verifying cross-border compliance clauses; or an investment analyst constructing a high-pressure valuation model

these workloads are not merely prompts to be answered, but context-heavy professional deliverables that require specialized knowledge, long-horizon execution, and strict adherence to domain constraints
The task is tested against state-of-the-art agents from different model families to minimize bias, and retained only if several agents fail to meet a predefined passing threshold based on rubrics.
these tasks are semi-open-ended, allowing different valid approaches, and are timeagnostic, yielding stable benchmarks over time
concurrent adversarial validation
the task undergoes an independent peer review by a second expert in the same sub-domain
a third expert performs an independent audit
Tasks with excessively low difficulty are removed.
Tasks with extreme difficulty, where agents consistently yield universally low scores, undergo a secondary review to avoid unanswerable or infeasible tasks.
$OneMillion-Bench consists of 5 macro domains, 37 sub-domains and 92 third-level categories

we propose a negative rubric scoring mechanism with asymmetric rubric weights ranging from -20 to 10 to better align with realistic domain requirements

the negative rubrics are mostly around behavioral violations of industrial norms or professional conduct, harmful generation, hallucination, and lapses in expected competencies such as instruction following
each effective rubric evaluation consists of four fundamental elements
Web Search: This evaluates the agentic ability to locate and extract factual information, entity facts, and authoritative definitions from retrieved sources.
and logical deductions, addressing questions of why and how.
Verbalization: This evaluates the organization, language style, and readability of the generation, ensuring clear, professional, and appropriate communication.
this assesses the adherence of agents to explicit constraints, rules, and guidance, ensuring controllable, predictable behaviors that meet user requirements
$OneMillion-Bench consists of 200 English and 200 Chinese instances
The Chinese (CN) set, however, is not a direct translation in parallelism to the Global set, but a purpose-built collection that incorporates tasks specific to the context of the China Mainland.
encompassing a total of 37 models and agents, which are grouped into three categories according to their characteristics
vanilla models (17 models): the vanilla models represent open-source and proprietary models evaluated without tool usage, including claude-opus-4.6
web search agents (vanilla models equipped with web search tools, 17 agents)
deep research agents (3 agents): these are specialized systems for long-horizon research, including o3-deepresearch [23], o4-mini-deepresearch [23], and sonar-deepresearch [29].

A rubric-based automated evaluation system for language agents capabilities on economically conceptual tasks across professional domains.
It evaluates 50+ models or agent systems from 6 API-based providers with weighted binary grading, async concurrency, cost tracking, and Excel/JSON reporting.
$OneMillion-Bench is a CLI tool ( omb ) that generates LLM agent responses, grades them against weighted rubrics using judge models, and produces reports.
